question_en: What are the manufacturer and specific model of the photography accessory shown in the image?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 2-2-F01

## Step 01 · Narrow down equipment scope from visible nameplates and mechanical structure

**Action:** Observe the Leitz logo, central ground glass, right-side camera mount, and black rectangular sliding rail structure in the input. Search query example: "Leitz sliding focusing copying attachment bayonet ground glass"; first look for device diagrams and original factory code tables.

**Evidence Observation:** The right-side connection shows a segmented bayonet mount, while the left-side housing and guide rails are relatively thick. The current image lacks the H-shaped spring clip common to similar devices. The absence of a detachable accessory itself does not rule out a specific model; judgment should combine the bayonet mount and main body structure.

## Step 02 · Retrieve photos corresponding to OOTGU

**Action:** Consult PHSC's "End of an era" and its original images, matching the housing, ground glass, right-side mount, and bottom rail in the problem image one by one.

Entry and OOTGU images:
https://phsc.ca/camera/end-of-an-era/

https://phsc.ca/camera/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/OOTGU.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The image layout matches the input's camera mount, central window, and thick housing. The article associates this device with OOTGU. At this point, a name candidate is obtained, but letter codes for photography accessories are easily confused, so continue to verify connection specifications using the original factory catalog.

## Step 03 · Differentiate OOTGU, OOBAZ, and other neighbors using the catalog

**Action:** Read the Leitz sliding focusing attachment description comparing OOTGU/OOBAZ, as well as the corresponding order codes in the original factory catalog. Focus on checking the combination of bayonet mounts, screw mounts, and spring clips.

Glissiere PDF page 2 OOTGU, page 3 OOBAZ:
https://www.summilux.net/documents/Glissiere.pdf

Original factory catalog (03695 PDF page 53/print page C8; 03919 PDF page 13/print page 11):
https://www.pacificrimcamera.com/rl/03695/03695.pdf

https://www.pacificrimcamera.com/rl/03919/03919.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The catalog links OOTGU / 16,680 with a bayonet-mount structure, while OOBAZ / 16,607 corresponds to a screw-mount camera installation method. OOBAZ also has a very similar housing and sliding rail, but its camera connection part and H-shaped clamping structure differ from the problem image. Early OOZAB references show different thin plates, curved ends, and clamping arms; the New York type 70.325 features a long horizontal arm and a thinner base plate, unlike the thick housing in the problem image.

Photos of similar OOBAZ, early accessory entries, and two references:
https://phsc.ca/camera/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/OOZAB-N-51mm.jpg

https://www.earlyphotography.co.uk/site/entry_M216.html

https://www.earlyphotography.co.uk/Images/M216.JPG

https://www.earlyphotography.co.uk/Images/M69.JPG

Collection entries and multi-angle photos:
https://kameramuseum.de/objekte/leitz-leica-sliding-focusing-copying-attachment-oozab/

https://kameramuseum.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/103352_Leitz_Copying-Attachment_Eisg-4c.jpg

https://kameramuseum.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/103352_Leitz_Copying-Attachment_Eisg-3b.jpg

New York equipment catalog (PDF page 45 relevant image):
https://www.pacificrimcamera.com/rl/04009/04009.pdf

## Step 04 · Resolve mixed letter codes and output manufacturer and model

**Action:** Cross-check recorded names against the Leitz letter code index, ensuring that set codes, single-item codes, or image filenames are not confused with one another.

Code index and PHSC comparison articles prone to mixed naming:
https://www.summilux.net/aide/lettre.php?lettre=O

https://phsc.ca/camera/a-new-day-dawns/

**Evidence Observation:** There is a risk of mixing OOZAB, OOBAZ, and OOGAN in comparison articles and image naming; OOGAN may refer to the entire assembly combination, so the appearance of this term on a webpage should not replace the specific accessory model. The manufacturer is Ernst Leitz, and the specific device model is OOTGU, supported by the bayonet structure, matching images, and the original factory catalog. It is not possible to derive a measurement of 51 mm from the image perspective, nor is it necessary to infer the serial number or configuration year.

**Stop Condition:** The name and structure correspond consistently; the question only asks for the manufacturer and model, so retain these two items.

## Formal Answer

Ernst Leitz；OOTGU
